source_arguments.name: RHTower.tendsto_primeRpowSumIoc
source_arguments.statement:
theorem tendsto_primeRpowSumIoc {a : ℝ} (ha0 : 0 < a) (ha1 : a < 1) :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => primeRpowSumIoc a x * (a * Real.log x) / x ^ a) atTop (nhds 1)
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem tendsto_primeRpowSumIoc {a : ℝ} (ha0 : 0 < a) (ha1 : a < 1) :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => primeRpowSumIoc a x * (a * Real.log x) / x ^ a) atTop (nhds 1)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  obtain ⟨g, hg, g_int, hθ⟩ := chebyshev_asymptotic''
  have hgt : Tendsto g atTop (nhds 0) :=
    (Asymptotics.isLittleO_one_iff ℝ).mp (hg 1 one_pos)
  have hJ := HTGeometry.tendsto_logRpowIntegral ha0
  have hK := HTGeometry.tendsto_logSqRpowIntegral ha0
  have hlogdiv : Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => Real.log x / x ^ a) atTop (nhds 0) :=
    (isLittleO_log_rpow_atTop ha0).tendsto_div_nhds_zero
  have hgint : ∀ x : ℝ, 2 ≤ x →
      IntervalIntegrable (fun t : ℝ => g t * abelKernel a t) volume 2 x := by
    intro x hx
    rw [intervalIntegrable_iff_integrableOn_Ioc_of_le hx]
    exact ((g_int x hx).mul_continuousOn
      (fun t ht => (continuousAt_abelKernel (a := a) ht.1).continuousWithinAt)
      isCompact_Icc).mono_set Ioc_subset_Icc_self
  -- the boundary term
  have hT1 : Tendsto
      (fun x : ℝ => rpowDivLog a x * Chebyshev.theta x * (a * Real.log x) / x ^ a) atTop
      (nhds a) := by
    have hlim : Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => a * (1 + g x)) atTop (nhds a) := by
      have h := (tendsto_const_nhds (x := a)).mul
        ((tendsto_const_nhds (x := (1 : ℝ))).add hgt)
      rw [add_zero, mul_one] at h
      exact h
    refine hlim.congr' ?_
    filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop (2 : ℝ)] with x hx
    have hx0 : (0 : ℝ) < x := by linarith
    have hlogx : 0 < Real.log x := Real.log_pos (by linarith)
    have hXpos : (0 : ℝ) < x ^ a := Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hx0 a
    have hsub : x ^ (a - 1) = x ^ a / x := by
      rw [Real.rpow_sub hx0, Real.rpow_one]
    rw [rpowDivLog, hθ x hx0, hsub]
    field_simp
  -- the fixed endpoint term
  have hT2 : Tendsto
      (fun x : ℝ => rpowDivLog a 2 * Chebyshev.theta 2 * (a * Real.log x) / x ^ a) atTop
      (nhds 0) := by
    have h := hlogdiv.const_mul (rpowDivLog a 2 * Chebyshev.theta 2 * a)
    rw [mul_zero] at h
    refine h.congr fun x => ?_
    ring
  -- the main integral
  have hmain : Tendsto
      (fun x : ℝ => (∫ t in (2 : ℝ)..x, abelKernel a t) * (a * Real.log x) / x ^ a) atTop
      (nhds (a - 1)) := by
    have hlim : Tendsto (fun x : ℝ =>
        (a - 1) * (HTGeometry.logRpowIntegral a x * (a * Real.log x) / x ^ a)
          - a * (HTGeometry.logSqRpowIntegral a x * Real.log x / x ^ a)) atTop
        (nhds (a - 1)) := by
      have h := (hJ.const_mul (a - 1)).sub (hK.const_mul a)
      rw [mul_one, mul_zero, sub_zero] at h
      exact h
    refine hlim.congr' ?_
    filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop (2 : ℝ)] with x hx
    rw [integral_abelKernel hx]
    ring
  -- the remainder
  have hrem := tendsto_abelRemainder ha0 hgt g_int
  -- assemble
  have hsum : Tendsto (fun x : ℝ =>
      rpowDivLog a x * Chebyshev.theta x * (a * Real.log x) / x ^ a
        - rpowDivLog a 2 * Chebyshev.theta 2 * (a * Real.log x) / x ^ a
        - ((∫ t in (2 : ℝ)..x, abelKernel a t) * (a * Real.log x) / x ^ a
          + (∫ t in (2 : ℝ)..x, g t * abelKernel a t) * (a * Real.log x) / x ^ a)) atTop
      (nhds (a - 0 - ((a - 1) + 0))) := (hT1.sub hT2).sub (hmain.add hrem)
  rw [show a - 0 - ((a - 1) + 0) = 1 by ring] at hsum
  refine hsum.congr' ?_
  filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop (2 : ℝ)] with x hx
  have hx0 : (0 : ℝ) < x := by linarith
  have hker : IntervalIntegrable (abelKernel a) volume 2 x :=
    intervalIntegrable_abelKernel a (le_refl (2 : ℝ)) hx
  have hdecomp : (∫ t in Ioc (2 : ℝ) x, deriv (rpowDivLog a) t * Chebyshev.theta t)
      = (∫ t in (2 : ℝ)..x, abelKernel a t) + ∫ t in (2 : ℝ)..x, g t * abelKernel a t := by
    rw [← intervalIntegral.integral_of_le hx, ← intervalIntegral.integral_add hker (hgint x hx)]
    refine intervalIntegral.integral_congr fun t ht => ?_
    have ht2 : (2 : ℝ) ≤ t := HTGeometry.two_le_of_mem_uIcc (le_refl (2 : ℝ)) hx ht
    have ht0 : (0 : ℝ) < t := by linarith
    rw [deriv_rpowDivLog ht2, hθ t ht0, abelKernel]
    ring
  rw [primeRpowSumIoc_eq hx, hdecomp]
  ring

method.description: The proof establishes the limit of a function involving Chebyshev's theta function and integral terms by decomposing and bounding components using asymptotic properties and integral convergence.

source_arguments.name: pi_asymp''
source_arguments.statement:
theorem pi_asymp'' :
    (fun x => ((Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ) / ∫ t in Set.Icc 2 x, 1 / log t) - (1 : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      fun _ => (1 : ℝ)
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem pi_asymp'' :
    (fun x => ((Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ) / ∫ t in Set.Icc 2 x, 1 / log t) - (1 : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      fun _ => (1 : ℝ)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  obtain ⟨f, hf, f_int, hf'⟩ := chebyshev_asymptotic''
  have eq1 : ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in atTop,
      ⌊x⌋₊.primeCounting =
      (log x)⁻¹ * (x + x * f x) +
      (∫ t in Set.Icc 2 x,
        (t + t * f t) * (t * log t ^ 2)⁻¹) := by
    filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop 2] with x hx
    rw [pi_asymp_aux x hx, hf' x (by linarith)]
    congr 1
    apply setIntegral_congr_fun measurableSet_Icc fun t ht ↦ ?_
    rw [hf' t (by grind)]

  replace eq1 :
    ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in atTop,
      ⌊x⌋₊.primeCounting =
      (log x)⁻¹ * (x + x * f x) +
      ((∫ t in Set.Icc 2 x, (log t ^ 2)⁻¹) +
        (∫ t in Set.Icc 2 x, (f t) * (log t ^ 2)⁻¹)) := by
    filter_upwards [eq1, eventually_ge_atTop 2] with x eq1 hx
    rw [eq1]
    congr
    simp_rw [mul_inv_rev, add_mul]
    rw [MeasureTheory.integral_add]
    · congr 1
      all_goals
        apply setIntegral_congr_fun measurableSet_Icc fun t ht ↦ ?_
        field [show t ≠ 0 by grind]
    · apply IntegrableOn.mul_continuousOn
        (hg := ContinuousOn.integrableOn_Icc <| continuousOn_id' _)
        (hK := isCompact_Icc)
      apply continuousOn_log1.mono ?_
      intro y h
      simp only [Set.mem_Icc, Set.mem_compl_iff, Set.mem_insert_iff,
        Set.mem_singleton_iff, not_or] at h ⊢
      exact ⟨by linarith, by linarith, by linarith⟩
    · rw [show (fun t ↦ t * f t * ((log t ^ 2)⁻¹ * t⁻¹)) =
        fun t ↦ f t * (t * (log t ^ 2)⁻¹ * t⁻¹) by ext; ring]
      apply IntegrableOn.mul_continuousOn (hK := isCompact_Icc)
      · apply f_int x (by linarith)
      · simp_rw [mul_assoc]
        refine ContinuousOn.mul (continuousOn_id' (Set.Icc 2 x)) ?_
        apply continuousOn_log1.mono ?_
        intro y h
        simp only [Set.mem_Icc, Set.mem_compl_iff, Set.mem_insert_iff,
          Set.mem_singleton_iff, not_or] at h ⊢
        exact ⟨by linarith, by linarith, by linarith⟩

  simp_rw [mul_add] at eq1
  simp_rw [show ∀ (x : ℝ),
    (log x)⁻¹ * x + (log x)⁻¹ * (x * f x) +
    ((∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Icc 2 x, (log t ^ 2)⁻¹) +
      ∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Icc 2 x, f t * (log t ^ 2)⁻¹) =
    ((log x)⁻¹ * x + (∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Icc 2 x, (log t ^ 2)⁻¹)) +
    ((log x)⁻¹ * (x * f x) +
      ∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Icc 2 x, f t * (log t ^ 2)⁻¹)
    by intros; ring] at eq1

  replace eq1 :
    ∃ (C : ℝ), ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in atTop,
      ⌊x⌋₊.primeCounting =
      (∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Icc 2 x, (log t)⁻¹) +
      ((log x)⁻¹ * (x * f x) +
        ∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Icc 2 x, f t * (log t ^ 2)⁻¹) +
      C := by
    use ((log 2)⁻¹ * 2)
    filter_upwards [eq1, eventually_ge_atTop 2] with x eq1 hx
    rw [eq1, ← integral_log_inv'' _ _ (by rfl) hx]
    ring
  replace eq1 :
    ∃ (C : ℝ), ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in atTop,
      (⌊x⌋₊.primeCounting / ∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Icc 2 x, (log t)⁻¹) - 1 =
      ((log x)⁻¹ * (x * f x) / (∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Icc 2 x, (log t)⁻¹) +
        (∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Icc 2 x, f t * (log t ^ 2)⁻¹) /
          (∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Icc 2 x, (log t)⁻¹)) +
      C / (∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Icc 2 x, (log t)⁻¹) := by
    obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := eq1
    use C
    filter_upwards [hC, eventually_gt_atTop 2] with x hC hx
    rw [hC]
    field [integral_log_inv_ne_zero]
  simp_rw [isLittleO_iff] at hf
  choose C hC using eq1
  simp_rw [← one_div] at hC
  apply isLittleO_congr hC (by rfl) |>.mpr
  have ineq1 (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) : ∀ᶠ(x : ℝ) in atTop,
    (log x)⁻¹ * x * |f x| ≤ c * ε * ((log x)⁻¹ * x) := by
    filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop 2, hf ε hε hc] with x hx hM
    simp only [norm_eq_abs] at hM
    rw [abs_of_pos hε] at hM
    rw [mul_comm (c * ε)]
    gcongr
    bound
  have int_flog {a b : ℝ} (ha: 2 ≤ a) (hb : 2 ≤ b) :
      IntegrableOn (fun t ↦ |f t| * (log t ^ 2)⁻¹) (Set.Icc a b) volume := by
    apply IntegrableOn.mul_continuousOn
    · apply Integrable.abs <| f_int b hb |>.mono (Set.Icc_subset_Icc_left ha) (by rfl)
    · refine ContinuousOn.inv₀ (ContinuousOn.pow (continuousOn_log |>.mono ?_) 2) ?_
      · simp
        grind
      · intro t ht
        simp only [Set.mem_Icc, ne_eq, OfNat.ofNat_ne_zero, not_false_eq_true,
          pow_eq_zero_iff, log_eq_zero, not_or] at ht ⊢

  have hg_dom : (fun t => deriv f t * ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 0 ⌊t⌋₊, vonMangoldt k) =O[atTop]

    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_mul, abs_mul, abs_neg,

  have hg_int : IntegrableAtFilter (fun t : ℝ => t ^ (-s)) atTop :=

      (𝓝 (∑' n : ℕ, vonMangoldt n / (n : ℝ) ^ s)) := by

### Parent overlap

- The endpoint ODE and fixed-mode asymptotics are classical prolate theory.
- The constants `8/11` and `16*pi/11` come from the repository's constrained source and endpoint
  theorems.
- Equation `(9)` is a change of variables in the exact leakage norm.

### Formula-level parent comparison

Dunster's radial approximation uses a Bessel argument `gamma*sqrt(eta)` with
`eta~2(1-sigma^2)(x-1)` at the radial endpoint. For fixed mode, `gamma=2*pi*lambda^2`, so its
classical inner scale is `x-1` of order `gamma^(-2)`, equivalently `y-lambda` of order
`lambda^(-3)`. The outer mass scale follows directly from the exact leakage norm and endpoint
height. Thus the scale separation is a useful constrained-source specialization of parent theory,
not a new asymptotic regime.

The constants `(10)` and `(14)` sharpen the CCM normalization and materially repair the route, but
the theorem fails the anti-theatre parent-interpolation gate after vocabulary erasure. It is
classified as a bridge. The candidate-new residue remains the arithmetic dilation constant in
`ccm-constrained-endpoint-euler-response-constant.md`.

# CCM first-clock asymptotic Bohr completeness

- **ID:** `ccm-first-clock-asymptotic-bohr-completeness`
- **Stage:** `3-formalized/needs-audit`

- **Status:** `[PAPER-PROVED] [LEAN-PROVED] [AXIOM-AUDITED] [NOVELTY UNVERIFIED] [NOT RH]`

- **Whole-corpus HT source:** `HTGeometry/SummableSpectrumScrewRecurrence.lean`

## Exact theorem

Let

```text
F(L) = L * ccmPublishedSourceSineCoefficient(L/2, 2*pi/L).
```

Then

```text
(exists continuous Bohr-almost-periodic P : R -> R,
  F(L)-P(L) -> 0 as L -> +infinity) <-> RiemannHypothesis.
```

Left side names only literal published CCM source. It contains no zero-location condition.

Under RH explicit witness is

```text
P(L) = 2 * sum_q (1-cos(gamma_q*L))/gamma_q^2,
gamma_q = Re(xiSpectralPoint q).
```

## New formal mathematics

1. Every nonnegative summable-frequency screw series is Bohr almost periodic, with no frequency
   independence or nonzero-frequency premise.
2. For `L >= 2*pi`, each first-clock moving-denominator term exceeds screw term and error is at most
   `(2/15)*(2*pi/L)^2/gamma_q^2`.
3. Summing over multiplicity-exact Xi divisor gives explicit `O(L^-2)` asymptote.
4. Every point of complete relation-hull interval is approximated by scaled literal source with
   bounded gaps after one threshold.
5. Absolute endpoint equals `4*sum_q gamma_q^-2` exactly when every finite integral relation among
   ordinates has even total coefficient. No simplicity or rational independence.

/-!
# The limiting time distribution of an asymptotic orbit

A path which is asymptotic to a phase flow sees the same time averages as the flow itself: the
difference tends to zero, and the running average of a function tending to zero tends to zero,
because the early part of the integral is bounded and the late part is uniformly small.

Along a rationally independent phase flow the running averages of a continuous function converge to
its Haar mean.  Hence for every continuous observable the time distribution of the asymptotic path
converges weakly to the push-forward of Haar measure under the parametrisation of the hull.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open GaloisForLFunctions

noncomputable section

variable {ι : Type*}

/-- **A vanishing function has vanishing running average.**  Beyond a fixed time the integrand is
uniformly small, and the bounded contribution of the initial segment is divided by the window
length. -/
theorem tendsto_windowAverage_zero_of_tendsto_zero {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hf : Continuous f)
    (hlim : Tendsto f atTop (nhds 0)) :
    Tendsto (windowAverage f) atTop (nhds 0) := by
  rw [NormedAddGroup.tendsto_nhds_zero] at hlim ⊢
  intro ε hε
  obtain ⟨t₀, ht₀⟩ := eventually_atTop.mp (hlim (ε / 4) (by linarith))
  set t₁ : ℝ := max t₀ 0 with ht₁def
  have ht₁nn : 0 ≤ t₁ := le_max_right _ _
  have ht₁ge : t₀ ≤ t₁ := le_max_left _ _
  obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := (isCompact_Icc (a := (0 : ℝ)) (b := t₁)).exists_bound_of_continuousOn
    hf.continuousOn
  have hCnn : 0 ≤ C := le_trans (norm_nonneg _) (hC 0 ⟨le_refl 0, ht₁nn⟩)
  have hint : ∀ a b : ℝ, IntervalIntegrable f volume a b := hf.intervalIntegrable
  filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop t₁, eventually_gt_atTop (0 : ℝ),
    eventually_gt_atTop (4 * C * t₁ / ε)] with T hT₁ hT0 hTbig
  have hsplit : (∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..t₁, f t) + ∫ t in t₁..T, f t = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..T, f t :=
    intervalIntegral.integral_add_adjacent_intervals (hint _ _) (hint _ _)
  have hb1 : ‖∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..t₁, f t‖ ≤ C * t₁ := by
    refine (intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const (C := C)
      fun x hx => ?_).trans ?_
    · rw [Set.uIoc_of_le ht₁nn] at hx
      exact hC x ⟨hx.1.le, hx.2⟩
    · rw [sub_zero, abs_of_nonneg ht₁nn]
  have hb2 : ‖∫ t in t₁..T, f t‖ ≤ ε / 4 * T := by
    refine (intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const (C := ε / 4)
      fun x hx => ?_).trans ?_
    · rw [Set.uIoc_of_le hT₁] at hx
      exact (ht₀ x (le_trans ht₁ge hx.1.le)).le
    · rw [abs_of_nonneg (by linarith)]

      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hle (by linarith)
  have hnorm : ‖windowAverage f T‖ ≤ C * t₁ / T + ε / 4 := by
    rw [windowAverage, ← hsplit, norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs,

/-!
# Canonical reconstruction and the complete collapsed-anchor fibre

The attainable weighted sources have a canonical finite inverse with zero blind-endpoint mass.
Every original source is exactly this inverse plus one free nonnegative endpoint mass. The
resulting equivalence separates reconstructible data from the discarded sector, as an
experimental corpus application of arXiv:2607.24901's reconstruction viewpoint.
-/

/-- Attainable collapsed-anchor weighted sources. -/
abbrev GomesClarkCollapsedImage :=
  {ν : FiniteMeasure HausdorffSourceSpace // ν ∈ Set.range (gomesClarkWeightedSource 0)}

/-- The attainable datum carried by a finite source. -/
def gomesClarkCollapsedImageOf (μ : FiniteMeasure HausdorffSourceSpace) : GomesClarkCollapsedImage :=
  ⟨gomesClarkWeightedSource 0 μ, ⟨μ, rfl⟩⟩

/-- The canonical finite inverse of an attainable datum. -/
def gomesClarkCollapsedSource (ν : GomesClarkCollapsedImage) : FiniteMeasure HausdorffSourceSpace :=
  ⟨gomesClarkCollapsedUnweight (ν.val : Measure HausdorffSourceSpace),
    (gomesClarkCollapsedUnweight_finite_iff _).mpr ((gomesClarkCollapsed_range_iff ν.val).mp ν.property).2⟩

/-- The canonical inverse recovers exactly the visible restriction of every original source. -/
theorem gomesClarkCollapsedSource_imageOf (μ : FiniteMeasure HausdorffSourceSpace) :
    gomesClarkCollapsedSource (gomesClarkCollapsedImageOf μ) = μ.restrict {gomesHausdorffOne}ᶜ := by
  apply FiniteMeasure.toMeasure_injective
  exact gomesClarkCollapsedUnweight_weight (μ : Measure HausdorffSourceSpace)

/-- The inverse reconstructs every attainable weighted source exactly. -/
theorem gomesClarkCollapsedSource_weighted (ν : GomesClarkCollapsedImage) :
    gomesClarkWeightedSource 0 (gomesClarkCollapsedSource ν) = ν.val := by
  obtain ⟨μ, hμ⟩ := ν.property
  have hv : ν = gomesClarkCollapsedImageOf μ := Subtype.ext hμ.symm
  rw [hv]
  apply FiniteMeasure.toMeasure_injective
  change gomesClarkCollapsedWeight
    (gomesClarkCollapsedUnweight (gomesClarkCollapsedWeight (μ : Measure HausdorffSourceSpace))) = _
  rw [gomesClarkCollapsedWeight_unweight]
  have hr := Measure.restrict_add_restrict_compl
    (μ := gomesClarkCollapsedWeight (μ : Measure HausdorffSourceSpace))
    (measurableSet_singleton gomesHausdorffOne)
  rw [Measure.restrict_eq_zero.mpr (gomesClarkCollapsedWeight_one _), zero_add] at hr
  exact hr

/-- The canonical inverse has no arbitrary blind-endpoint contribution. -/
theorem gomesClarkCollapsedSource_one (ν : GomesClarkCollapsedImage) :
    gomesClarkCollapsedSource ν {gomesHausdorffOne} = 0 := by
  change (gomesClarkCollapsedUnweight (ν.val : Measure HausdorffSourceSpace)
    {gomesHausdorffOne}).toNNReal = 0
  rw [gomesClarkCollapsedUnweight_one]
  rfl

/-- Weighting the canonical inverse restores its attainable datum, including the range witness. -/
theorem gomesClarkCollapsedImageOf_source (ν : GomesClarkCollapsedImage) :
    gomesClarkCollapsedImageOf (gomesClarkCollapsedSource ν) = ν :=
  Subtype.ext (gomesClarkCollapsedSource_weighted ν)

/-- Every finite source splits into its canonical inverse and its exact missing endpoint mass. -/
theorem gomesClarkCollapsedSource_decomposition (μ : FiniteMeasure HausdorffSourceSpace) :
    μ = gomesClarkCollapsedSource (gomesClarkCollapsedImageOf μ) +
      μ {gomesHausdorffOne} • gomesHausdorffOneAtom := by
  rw [gomesClarkCollapsedSource_imageOf]
  apply FiniteMeasure.toMeasure_injective
  rw [FiniteMeasure.toMeasure_add, FiniteMeasure.restrict_measure_eq, FiniteMeasure.toMeasure_smul]
  change (μ : Measure HausdorffSourceSpace) = (μ : Measure HausdorffSourceSpace).restrict
    {gomesHausdorffOne}ᶜ + (μ {gomesHausdorffOne} : ℝ≥0∞) • Measure.dirac gomesHausdorffOne
  rw [FiniteMeasure.ennreal_coeFn_eq_coeFn_toMeasure, ← Measure.restrict_singleton]
  exact (Measure.restrict_compl_add_restrict (measurableSet_singleton _)).symm

/-- Adding any endpoint-one mass leaves the weighted datum unchanged. -/
theorem gomesClarkCollapsedWeighted_oneCompletion (μ : FiniteMeasure HausdorffSourceSpace)
    (w : ℝ≥0) :
    gomesClarkWeightedSource 0 (μ + w • gomesHausdorffOneAtom) = gomesClarkWeightedSource 0 μ := by
  apply (gomesClarkAnchorRecord_eq_iff_weighted 0 0 _ _).mp
  rw [gomesClarkAnchorRecord_zero, gomesClarkAnchorRecord_zero]
  exact gomesClarkFixedRecord_oneCompletion μ w

/-- The attainable datum is unchanged by every blind-endpoint completion. -/
theorem gomesClarkCollapsedImageOf_oneCompletion (μ : FiniteMeasure HausdorffSourceSpace)
    (w : ℝ≥0) :
    gomesClarkCollapsedImageOf (μ + w • gomesHausdorffOneAtom) = gomesClarkCollapsedImageOf μ :=
  Subtype.ext (gomesClarkCollapsedWeighted_oneCompletion μ w)

/-- **Finite composable-path normal form.**  The genuine Gram word of a path is compactly equal
to the unique window determined by its first endpoint, last endpoint, and minimum visited scale. -/
theorem operator_compactEq_window (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) :
    ∀ P : SoninScalePath, P.operator a =ₖ (P.window a ha).operator
  | .edge p q hp hq => by
      have h := (soninGramFactorOfScales p q hp hq).operator_compactEq_liveWindow a ha
      rw [soninGramFactor_liveWindow_eq_pathWindow a p q ha hp hq] at h
      simpa [SoninScalePath.operator, SoninScalePath.window, start, endpoint, minimum] using h
  | .extend P r hr => by
      let e := soninPathWindow a P.endpoint r (min P.endpoint r) ha
        P.endpoint_gt_one hr (lt_min P.endpoint_gt_one hr)
        (min_le_left P.endpoint r) (min_le_right P.endpoint r)
      let g := soninGramFactorOfScales P.endpoint r P.endpoint_gt_one hr
      have hedge := soninGramFactor_liveWindow_eq_pathWindow
        a P.endpoint r ha P.endpoint_gt_one hr
      have hnext : g.operator a =ₖ e.operator := by
        have h := g.operator_compactEq_liveWindow a ha
        change g.operator a =ₖ (g.liveWindow a ha).operator at h
        rw [hedge] at h
        exact h
      have hmul : P.operator a * g.operator a =ₖ (P.window a ha).operator * e.operator :=
        CompactOperatorEq.mul (operator_compactEq_window a ha P) hnext
      have hstate := soninWindowState_operator_mul_compactEq ha
        (SoninWindowState.live (P.window a ha)) (SoninWindowState.live e)
      dsimp only [window, e, composeSoninWindowStates] at hstate
      rw [composeSoninPathWindows a P.start P.endpoint r P.minimum
        (min P.endpoint r) ha P.start_gt_one P.endpoint_gt_one hr
        P.minimum_gt_one (lt_min P.endpoint_gt_one hr)
        P.minimum_le_start P.minimum_le_endpoint
        (min_le_left P.endpoint r) (min_le_right P.endpoint r)] at hstate
      have hmin : min P.minimum (min P.endpoint r) = min P.minimum r := by
        rw [← min_assoc, min_eq_left P.minimum_le_endpoint]
      have hwindow :
          soninPathWindow a P.start r (min P.minimum (min P.endpoint r)) ha
              P.start_gt_one hr (lt_min P.minimum_gt_one (lt_min P.endpoint_gt_one hr))
              ((min_le_left P.minimum (min P.endpoint r)).trans P.minimum_le_start)
              ((min_le_right P.minimum (min P.endpoint r)).trans (min_le_right P.endpoint r)) =
            (SoninScalePath.extend P r hr).window a ha := by
        apply SoninLiveWindow.ext_coordinates
        · rfl
        · change (P.start * (min P.minimum (min P.endpoint r))⁻¹) * a =
            (P.start * (min P.minimum r)⁻¹) * a
          rw [hmin]
        · rfl
      rw [hwindow] at hstate
      exact hmul.trans hstate

/-- With fixed endpoints, the path-window datum recovers its minimum scale exactly. -/
theorem pathWindow_eq_iff_minimum_eq
    (a p q m n : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hp : 1 < p) (hq : 1 < q)
    (hm : 1 < m) (hn : 1 < n)
    (hmp : m ≤ p) (hmq : m ≤ q) (hnp : n ≤ p) (hnq : n ≤ q) :
    soninPathWindow a p q m ha hp hq hm hmp hmq =
        soninPathWindow a p q n ha hp hq hn hnp hnq ↔
      m = n := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hfloor := congrArg SoninLiveWindow.floor h
    change (p * m⁻¹) * a = (p * n⁻¹) * a at hfloor
    have hratio : p * m⁻¹ = p * n⁻¹ := mul_right_cancel₀ ha.ne' hfloor
    have hinv : m⁻¹ = n⁻¹ :=
      mul_left_cancel₀ (zero_lt_one.trans hp).ne' hratio
    exact inv_injective hinv
  · rintro rfl
    rfl

/-- Every finite composable Gram path remains noncompact: its minimum scale is strictly larger
than one, so its canonical shell never degenerates. -/
theorem operator_not_isCompactOperator (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (P : SoninScalePath) :
    ¬ IsCompactOperator (P.operator a) := by
  intro hcompact
  have hwindow : IsCompactOperator (P.window a ha).operator :=
    RHTower.IsCompactOperator.compactEq_right hcompact (P.operator_compactEq_window a ha)
  exact (P.window a ha).not_isCompactOperator ha hwindow

Gram entry between its endpoints exactly when no interior scale lies below both endpoints. -/
theorem operator_compactEq_direct_iff_minimum_eq_endpointMin

    P.operator a =ₖ

source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hn0 : (0 : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) := by
    have : (0 : ℕ) < n := by omega
    exact_mod_cast this
  have hninv : (0 : ℝ) < (n : ℝ)⁻¹ := by positivity
  have hle : (n : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ 1 := by
    rw [inv_le_one₀ hn0]
    exact_mod_cast Nat.one_le_of_lt (by omega : 1 < n)
  have hsub : Set.Icc ((n : ℝ)⁻¹) 1 ∩ Set.Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1 = Set.Icc ((n : ℝ)⁻¹) 1 := by
    apply Set.inter_eq_self_of_subset_left
    intro x hx
    exact ⟨lt_of_lt_of_le hninv hx.1, hx.2⟩
  rw [MeasureTheory.integral_indicator measurableSet_Icc, Measure.restrict_restrict measurableSet_Icc,
    hsub]
  have hIcc : ∫ x in Set.Icc ((n : ℝ)⁻¹) 1, x⁻¹ = ∫ x in ((n : ℝ)⁻¹)..1, x⁻¹ := by
    rw [intervalIntegral.integral_of_le hle, MeasureTheory.integral_Icc_eq_integral_Ioc]
  rw [hIcc]
  have hzero : (0 : ℝ) ∉ Set.uIcc ((n : ℝ)⁻¹) 1 := by
    rw [Set.uIcc_of_le hle]
    intro hmem
    exact absurd hmem.1 (not_le.mpr hninv)
  rw [integral_inv hzero]
  rw [one_div, inv_inv]

      ccmGuinandWeilThirdGradePrimeDirichletCoeff b k) *

  have hchange := MeasureTheory.integral_image_eq_integral_abs_deriv_smul
    (s := Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ)) (f := Real.exp) (f' := Real.exp) measurableSet_Ioi
    (fun x _ => Real.hasDerivAt_exp x |>.hasDerivWithinAt)

        ccmGuinandWeilThirdGradePrimeDirichletCoeff b k) *
          (t : ℂ) ^ (-(u + 1))) = _

      calc
        (Real.exp H : ℂ) *
            ((ccmGuinandWeilPrimeThirdGradeRateWindow b H : ℂ) *

            ((Real.exp H : ℂ) *
              (Real.exp H : ℂ) ^ (-(u + 1))) *

prose.text:
overlap-safe partition theorem. Under the explicit dyadic product window and
`sigma0 + eta + epsilon^2/20 <= 7/32 - 5 epsilon`, it proves

```text
sum_{t in S} |M1(1+it)|^2 |M2(1+it)|^2
  <= 16384 B1^2 (1+|log T|) C2^2
       (2(1+|log T|))^(2^(2(w2+1))-1)
     + T^(-epsilon^2/20) + T^(-1/2).
```

This is the dependency-closed finite Huxley-strength core, not the paper's literal measurable-set
Proposition 4.2. Two obligations remain distinct: the paper uses Jutila's sharper large-values
input, and its reduction from an arbitrary measurable `U subset [0,T]` to one-spaced samples needs
a restricted-set discretisation theorem. Corpus `exists_spaced_families_integral_le` applies only
to a continuous integrand on a full interval, so it cannot be used on `U.indicator F` without a
new measurable-set argument. No measurable conclusion is claimed.

### M2, brick 26 — exact pointwise two-window Perron comparison (2026-08-28)

Added `Sieve/MatomakiTeravainenLemma31PerronComparison.lean`. For natural left endpoint `A`, short
width `H`, reference width `H1`, coefficient cutoff `M`, and Perron height `T`, the theorem
`norm_perronWindowSum_compare_sub_integral_le` proves exactly

```text
windowSum(A,H) - (H/H1) windowSum(A,H1)
  = (1/(2*pi)) integral_{-T}^{T}
      perronPoly(1+it) perronCompareKernel(A+1/2,H,H1,t) dt
    + endpoint error,
```

with the endpoint error bounded by the sum of the two short-window Perron errors plus `H/H1`
times the two long-window Perron errors. The kernel identity is literal at base `A+1/2`; no
asymptotic notation, floor suppression, or cancellation premise is hidden. Existing
`norm_perronCompareKernel_le_min3` and `integral_mixed_moment_windowCompare_le` can now consume the
integral without another algebraic bridge.

This closes the pointwise Perron bookkeeping seam, not all of Lemma 3.1. Remaining work is the
continuous `x`-variance integration: align real window endpoints with the natural half-integer
windows, identify the coefficient polynomial with `P1(s)P(s)`, integrate the explicit endpoint
errors, and insert the assumed mixed mean-square bound. No variance conclusion is claimed yet.

### M6, brick 27 — cell-max discretisation *restricted to a closed set* (2026-08-29)

Brick 25 left `exists_matomakiTeravainen_typeII_proposition42_huxley` stated for finite one-spaced
frequency **sets**, and recorded that the passage to the paper's measurable `U ⊆ [0,T]` was blocked:
the corpus's `HTGeometry/CellMaxDiscretisation.exists_spaced_families_integral_le` discretises a
continuous integrand over a *full* interval, and its sample points are unconstrained, whereas the
Proposition 4.2 hypotheses require every sample point to satisfy the amplitude threshold — i.e. to
lie in `U`.

That gap is now closed, in the form the application actually needs.  `U` is not an arbitrary
measurable set: it is the set where a Dirichlet-polynomial amplitude exceeds a threshold, i.e. the
preimage of a closed half-line under a continuous function, hence **closed**.  For a closed
restricting set the cell-max argument runs verbatim, because each closed cell meets `U` in a
*compact* set and a continuous integrand attains its maximum there at a point of `U`.

`formal/GaloisForLFunctions/HTGeometry/CellMaxSetDiscretisation.lean`, unconditional and axiom-clean
(`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`), wired into `GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry`:

```text
iUnion_Ioc_cells                  the half-open cells of length Δ tile `Ioc a (a+mΔ)`
exists_cell_max_setIntegral_le    ∃ K ⊆ range m and maximisers c k ∈ U ∩ cell k with
                                    ∫_{U ∩ Ioc a (a+mΔ)} F ≤ ∑_{k ∈ K} Δ · F (c k)
exists_spaced_families_setIntegral_le
    ∃ S₁ S₂ ⊆ U ∩ Icc a (a+mΔ), both Δ-spaced, with
      ∫_{U ∩ Ioc a (a+mΔ)} F ≤ Δ · ( ∑_{S₁} F + ∑_{S₂} F )
```

The conclusion also records `S₁, S₂ ⊆ Icc a (a+mΔ)`, which discharges Proposition 4.2's diameter
hypothesis `∀ x y ∈ S, |x − y| ≤ 2T` at `a = -T`, `Δ = 1`, `m = 2T`.

Only cells that actually meet `U` enter the sum (the index set `K`), so no sample point is
manufactured outside the level set; cells missing `U` contribute a vanishing integral.  Splitting
`K` by parity gives the two `Δ`-spaced families.

**What this unblocks.** With the amplitude's continuity, the level set
`{t : A₁^{-σ₀} ≤ amp₁ t ∨ A₂^{-σ₀} ≤ amp₂ t}` is closed, and
`exists_spaced_families_setIntegral_le` converts the finite-set bound of brick 25 into a bound on
`∫_U amp₁² amp₂²` at the cost of a factor two.  That is the paper's Proposition 4.2 in integral
form, the shape §5's Cauchy–Schwarz consumes.

### M4d, brick 28 — Proposition 4.2 in integral form (2026-08-29)

`Sieve/MatomakiTeravainenProposition42Integral.lean`, unconditional and axiom-clean, wired into
`GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower`:

```text
continuous_matomakiTeravainenDirichletAmplitude
    the Dirichlet amplitude is continuous in the ordinate (from the corpus's `continuous_dirPoly`)
matomakiTeravainenTypeIIRegion T N₁ a₁ N₂ a₂ A₁ A₂ σ₀ B₁

try said was missing.  In the Halász application `S` is the window around
the exceptional frequency: on `S` the third factor has only its trivial bound `M₁ ≍ log N`, but `S` has measure
`O(δ/log z)` so the mean squares over `S` are small; off `S` the factor is damped, `M₂ ≍ e^{−δ²}·log N`.  Neither
piece uses the trivial bound over the whole range, which is what made the previous accounting collapse.

The pieces to supply now are the two corpus facts the corpus's own assembly already uses:
`norm_tsum_twistedSummand_le_of_far` for `M₂` and `volume_halaszLargeValues_le` for the measure of `S` — with the
mean square over `S` bounded by the window mean value theorem at width `|S|` rather than at width `T`.

## The mean square over a short set

`HTGeometry/WeightedHolder.lean` and `RHTower/Sieve/LSeriesTrivialSize.lean` (both green, axiom-clean).

* `integral_normSq_le_measure_mul_sq` — for any measure and any set of finite measure,
  `∫_S ‖g‖² ∂μ ≤ μ.real S · B²` when `‖g‖ ≤ B`.  No nonnegativity of `B` is needed: it follows at any point of
  `S`, and on the empty set both sides vanish.
* `integral_normSq_LSeries_le_measure` — the instance for a finitely supported series, with `B` the `ℓ¹` mass of
  the damped coefficients.

This is the estimate that turns "the exceptional window is short" into a saving, and it completes the two
ingredients of the split:

| piece | bound on `L(f)` | bound on the mean squares |
|---|---|---|
| `S` = large-value set ∩ `[−T,T]` | trivial, `(1+1/(σ−1))e^{7/2}` | `volume.real S · (ℓ¹)²` — small because `S` is short (`volume_halaszLargeValues_le`) |
| `Sᶜ` | damped, `…e^{−δ²}` — **by definition of `S`** | window mean value theorem at width `T` |

Note the economy on the complement: `S` is *defined* as the set where the damped bound fails, so on `Sᶜ` that
bound holds definitionally and `norm_tsum_twistedSummand_le_of_far` is not needed at the point of use — it is
what makes `S` small, inside `volume_halaszLargeValues_le`.

What remains is to instantiate `norm_integral_mul_three_le_split` with this `S`, which needs the measurability of
the large-value set (its defining inequality is continuous in `t`, so it is open in the subspace, hence
measurable) and the arithmetic of choosing `δ` against `logSqWeight z`.

## The large-value window as a measurable set

`RHTower/Sieve/HalaszWindowMeasurable.lean` (green, axiom-clean, wired).

* `isOpen_halaszLargeValues`, `measurableSet_halaszLargeValues` — the exceptional set
  `{t | (damped bound) < ‖L(f,σ+it)‖}` is a strict inequality between a constant and a continuous function of
  the frequency (`continuous_tsum_twistedSummand`), hence open and measurable;
* `volume_inter_Icc_ne_top` — intersected with a bounded height range it has finite measure;
* `norm_tsum_twistedSummand_le_of_not_mem` — off the set the damped bound holds, by definition of the set.

These are exactly the side conditions `norm_integral_mul_three_le_split` requires: a measurable `S`, finite
measure, and a bound on the third factor on each piece.  **Every ingredient of the dichotomy-shaped assembly is
now present:**

| ingredient | theorem |
|---|---|
| the split itself | `norm_integral_mul_three_le_split` |
| `S` measurable, finite | this module |
| damped bound off `S` | this module (definitional) |
| measure of `S` | `volume_halaszLargeValues_le` (corpus) |
| mean square on `S` | `integral_normSq_LSeries_le_measure` |
| mean square off `S` | `integral_Icc_normSq_LSeries_le_prime_sieve` |
| uniform kernel bound | `norm_perronKernel_le` |
| Perron identity | `tsum_mul_smoothWeight_ghs_eq_integral` |

The next step is the assembly, and then the accounting — which this time has the `e^{−δ²}` saving off the window
and the factor `volume S ≍ (T log z/π + 1)·δ/√(logSqWeight z)` on it, the two quantities that the previous
accounting lacked entirely.

## The dichotomy split, assembled

`RHTower/Sieve/DichotomySplitAssembly.lean` (green, axiom-clean, wired).

`norm_integral_Icc_mul_three_le_dichotomy` — for **any** threshold `c ≥ 0`, with `S` the set of heights where the
```

# Integral multiplicative periodic gear-count universality law

## Status

Formalized in Lean and wired into the RHTower umbrella. Kept in progress until global exhaustion
and final audit complete.

## Lean sources

## Conjecture

For every finite bound, one integral multiplicative degree-zero functional-equation carrier has
at least that many distinct real parts strictly between `0` and `1/2`, and through every selected
real part its zero set contains a full two-sided vertical arithmetic progression.

Thus integrality, multiplicativity, finite Dirichlet support, and the exact functional equation
do not merely permit unboundedly many off-line zero locations: they permit unboundedly many
distinct off-critical periodic zero combs in one carrier.

## Corpus gap

The gear-count theorem produces arbitrarily many distinct real off-line zeros. The periodicity
dichotomy theorem says every zero of every integral multiplicative FE carrier enters a full
vertical progression. No theorem applies the dichotomy simultaneously to the entire unbounded
gear set.

## Proof plan

1. Take the carrier and finite real zero set from the gear-count theorem.
2. Apply the class-wide periodicity dichotomy at each selected zero.
3. Exclude the critical-line branch using `σ < 1/2`.
4. Retain the progression period separately for every selected real part.

No numerical computation is used.

## Novelty status

Post-proof searches found general work on zeros and almost-periodicity of Dirichlet polynomials,
Dirichlet series satisfying Riemann-type functional equations, and nonvanishing of classical
`L`-functions on vertical arithmetic progressions. No searched source stated the exact unbounded
simultaneous zero-comb theorem for integral multiplicative finite-support coefficient streams
with the degree-zero functional equation. Novelty claim is restricted to that precise class and
construction.

# Actual density of the Maass current measure

- **ID:** SELBERG-CURRENT-DENSITY-IDENTIFICATION
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (Lean)
- **Parent:** [Original source currents](../1-in-progress/selberg-original-source-conserved-currents.md), [proved positive measure split](selberg-current-nodal-measures.md), Selberg cycle 40 continuation.
- **Objective:** Identify the actual current measure with its source density, retaining the separately proved nodal residual; continue toward the unchanged unconditional Selberg quarter bound.

## Source-derived theorem

Write D for the original trace density, C for the pair-plus-phase square numerator, and R_e=sqrt(D+e²). The proved regulated current is C/R_e³. The representing current measure equals hyperbolic volume weighted by y²*C/(sqrt(D))³, with value zero at original common zeros. Every compact-test density product is genuinely integrable, and the actual current integrals converge to its literal integral. The current and residual are mutually singular, are the restrictions of full curvature to the complement of the original nodal set and to that set, and are each modular invariant. These are identifications of existing source measures, not new endpoint hypotheses.

## Dependency-closed paper proof

At D>0, continuity of the positive square root makes R_e³ tend to the nonzero amplitude cube. At D=0, the original source theorem gives C=0, so the regulated current and the literal division-defined density are both zero. Tests vanish outside the upper half-plane, so their pointwise convergence holds on the entire plane even though source regularity is only local to the chart.

Take e_n=1/(n+1), with positivity, antitonicity, and convergence to the actual positive-regulator filter proved. For each nonnegative compact continuous test phi, the products phi*C/R_e_n³ are integrable, nonnegative, and monotone in n. Their integrals are bounded by the original finite full-curvature value L(phi). Extended-real monotone convergence shows that the integrals of their ENNReal.ofReal values converge to the extended integral of phi*C/(sqrt(D))³. The genuine regulated integrability identifies each prelimit extended integral with ofReal of its real integral. Passing the source bound to the limit gives an upper bound ofReal(L(phi)), strictly below infinity. Pointwise convergence of the measurable approximants proves measurability of the limit too. These two facts establish genuine density integrability.

Apply this to |phi|. It is again a continuous compact test with the same supported chart. Its integrable density product dominates the norm of every signed regulated product, including at original zeros. Dominated convergence along the actual countably generated positive-regulator filter identifies the full signed-test limit with the literal density integral. Comparison with the already proved currentMeasure compact-test limit proves equality of their pairings. No local convergence is promoted to a global mass assertion.

Define h(z)=y²*C/(sqrt(D))³ on the actual upper half-plane. Local continuity of C and amplitude makes their quotient measurable even at zeros; h is nonnegative. Set nu=volume.withDensity(ofReal h). The chart pushforward and the withDensity integrability theorem prove that y²*F on the upper half-plane is integrable exactly when F is integrable on the positive-height planar region. Thus every compact test is genuinely integrable for nu by the preceding density-product theorem. The integral chart identity cancels the y² factor against hyperbolic density y^-2 and gives the same planar density pairing.

For each compact K, choose an actual nonnegative compact continuous cutoff g equal to one on K. Its proved nu-integrability gives nu(K)<=ofReal(integral g dnu)<infinity. Hence nu is finite on compact sets and regular on the actual metrizable sigma-compact upper half-plane. Regular-measure uniqueness identifies nu with currentMeasure. Its definition proves absolute continuity relative to hyperbolic volume. On the literal nodal set h=0, so the withDensity measure vanishes there independently of that set's area. The already proved residual measure vanishes on the complement. This supplies a measurable separator proving mutual singularity of the two source measures.

This does not yet establish residual singularity relative to volume. In particular, current absolute continuity plus residual concentration on the nodal set is not a full Lebesgue-decomposition certificate without further control of that set or residual measure.

/-!
# Splitting a real integral into the two half-lines

`∫_ℝ F = ∫_0^∞ F(u) du + ∫_0^∞ F(-u) du` for integrable `F`.  This is the reflection step that
turns a pairing against the `χ`-kernel `(-2πui)^{s-1}` — which takes different branch values on the
two half-lines — into a single Mellin integral, once the other factor is even
(Burnol, arXiv:math/0203120).

## Main results

* `integral_eq_add_reflect`
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open MeasureTheory Set

noncomputable section

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]

theorem map_neg_restrict_Ioi_zero :
    ((volume : Measure ℝ).restrict (Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ))).map Neg.neg
      = (volume : Measure ℝ).restrict (Set.Iio (0 : ℝ)) := by
  conv_rhs => rw [← Measure.map_neg_eq_self (volume : Measure ℝ),
    measurableEmbedding_neg.restrict_map]
  congr 1
  ext x
  simp

theorem integral_Iio_zero_eq_integral_Ioi_neg (F : ℝ → E) :
    (∫ u in Set.Iio (0 : ℝ), F u) = ∫ u in Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ), F (-u) := by
  rw [← map_neg_restrict_Ioi_zero, measurableEmbedding_neg.integral_map]

/-- **Splitting a real integral into the two half-lines.** -/
theorem integral_eq_add_reflect {F : ℝ → E} (hint : Integrable F volume) :
    (∫ u : ℝ, F u) = (∫ u in Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ), F u) + ∫ u in Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ), F (-u) := by
  have hcompl := MeasureTheory.integral_add_compl (s := Set.Ioi (0:ℝ))
    (measurableSet_Ioi) hint
  have hIic : (Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ))ᶜ = Set.Iic (0 : ℝ) := by
    ext x
    simp
  rw [hIic] at hcompl
  have hIicIio : (∫ u in Set.Iic (0 : ℝ), F u) = ∫ u in Set.Iio (0 : ℝ), F u := by
    refine MeasureTheory.setIntegral_congr_set ?_
    exact Iio_ae_eq_Iic.symm
  rw [hIicIio, integral_Iio_zero_eq_integral_Ioi_neg] at hcompl
  exact hcompl.symm

end

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-!
# Cyclic algebras at finite residue extensions

At a finite residue extension, every cyclic degree-two parameter is a norm.  The corresponding
raw cyclic quotient is therefore a central simple algebra representing the split Brauer class.
This is the algebra-level residue component of local reciprocity; it deliberately does not lift
the residue algebra through a valuation ring to a local-field Brauer class.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.ABHN

attribute [local instance] Ideal.Quotient.field

variable {A B G : Type}
  [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
  [Group G] [Finite G] [MulSemiringAction G B] [SMulCommClass G A B]
  [Algebra.IsInvariant A B G]
  (P : Ideal A) (Q : Ideal B) [P.IsMaximal] [Q.IsMaximal] [Q.LiesOver P]
  [Finite (B ⧸ Q)]

/-- Every degree-two cyclic parameter at a finite residue extension vanishes in cohomology. -/
theorem residue_cyclicGaloisH2BaseProjection_eq_zero (a : Additive (A ⧸ P)ˣ) :
    cyclicGaloisH2BaseProjection (A ⧸ P) (B ⧸ Q) a = 0 :=
  finiteField_cyclicGaloisH2BaseProjection_eq_zero (A ⧸ P) (B ⧸ Q) a

/-- Every degree-two cyclic parameter at a finite residue extension is an actual norm. -/
theorem residue_cyclicGaloisH2BaseParameter_exists_norm (a : Additive (A ⧸ P)ˣ) :
    ∃ c : (B ⧸ Q)ˣ, (a.toMul : A ⧸ P) = Algebra.norm (A ⧸ P) (c : B ⧸ Q) :=
  finiteField_cyclicGaloisH2BaseParameter_exists_norm (A ⧸ P) (B ⧸ Q) a

/-- The raw cyclic algebra attached to a finite residue-field parameter is central simple. -/
noncomputable def residueCyclicGaloisAlgebraCSA (a : Additive (A ⧸ P)ˣ) : CSA (A ⧸ P) :=
  finiteField_cyclicGaloisAlgebraCSA (A ⧸ P) (B ⧸ Q) a

/-- Every residue cyclic algebra at a finite residue extension has split Brauer class. -/
theorem residue_brauerClass_cyclicGaloisAlgebraCSA_eq_split (a : Additive (A ⧸ P)ˣ) :
    brauerClass (residueCyclicGaloisAlgebraCSA P Q a) = brauerSplitClass (A ⧸ P) :=
  finiteField_brauerClass_cyclicGaloisAlgebraCSA_eq_split (A ⧸ P) (B ⧸ Q) a

/-- `split_ifs` splits the main goal in two goals for every if-then-else expression it contains,
by applying excluded middle to the condition. If the goal has the form `g (if p then x else y)`,
`split_ifs` will result in two goals `h✝ : p ⊢ g x` and `h✝ : ¬p ⊢ g y`. If there are multiple
if-then-else expressions, then `split_ifs` will split them all, starting with a top-most one whose
condition does not contain another if-then-else expression.

* `split_ifs with h₁ h₂ h₃` names the introduced hypotheses.
  Note that names are not reused across splits: on a goal of the form
  `⊢ (if p then 1 else 2) + (if q then 3 else 4)`, use `split_ifs with hp hq hq` to name all
  the hypotheses.
* `split_ifs at l` splits the if-then-else expressions at location(s) `l`.
-/
syntax (name := splitIfs) "split_ifs" (location)? (" with" (ppSpace colGt binderIdent)+)? : tactic

elab_rules : tactic
| `(tactic| split_ifs $[$loc:location]? $[with $withArg*]?) =>
  let loc := match loc with
  | none => Location.targets #[] true
  | some loc => expandLocation loc
  let names := match withArg with
  | none => []
  | some args => args.toList
  withMainContext do
    let names ← IO.mkRef names
    splitIfsCore loc names []
    for name in ← names.get do
      logWarningAt name m!"unused name: {name}"

end Mathlib.Tactic

representative-level construction. -/
theorem rationalFunctionLocalBrauerMap_brauerClass (F : Type u) [Field F] [Finite F]
    (A : CSA.{u, u} (RatFunc F)) :
    rationalFunctionLocalBrauerMap F (brauerClass A) =
      rationalFunctionLocalBrauerClassesOfCSA F A := by
  funext v
  rfl

/-- The rational-function-field global-to-local map sends the split global class to the
everywhere-split local family. -/
theorem rationalFunctionLocalBrauerMap_split (F : Type u) [Field F] [Finite F] :
    rationalFunctionLocalBrauerMap F (brauerSplitClass (RatFunc F)) =
      (rationalFunctionRestrictedSplitClass F).toLocalBrauerClasses := by
  funext v
  change scalarExtensionBrauerMap (RatFunc F) (rationalFunctionCompletion F v)
      (brauerSplitClass (RatFunc F)) = brauerSplitClass (rationalFunctionCompletion F v)
  exact scalarExtensionBrauerMap_split (RatFunc F) (rationalFunctionCompletion F v)

/-- Rational-function-field localization preserves tensor-product addition pointwise at every
place. -/
theorem rationalFunctionLocalBrauerMap_tensorAdd (F : Type u) [Field F] [Finite F]
    (x y : BrauerGroup.{u, u} (RatFunc F)) :
    rationalFunctionLocalBrauerMap F (brauerTensorAdd (RatFunc F) x y) = fun v ↦
      brauerTensorAdd (rationalFunctionCompletion F v)
        (rationalFunctionLocalBrauerMap F x v) (rationalFunctionLocalBrauerMap F y v) := by
  funext v
  exact scalarExtensionBrauerMap_tensorAdd (RatFunc F) (rationalFunctionCompletion F v) x y

/-- The rational-function-field global-to-local Brauer map as an additive homomorphism. -/
noncomputable def rationalFunctionLocalBrauerAddHom (F : Type u) [Field F] [Finite F] :
    BrauerGroup.{u, u} (RatFunc F) →+ rationalFunctionLocalBrauerClasses F where
  toFun := rationalFunctionLocalBrauerMap F
  map_zero' := rationalFunctionLocalBrauerMap_split F
  map_add' := rationalFunctionLocalBrauerMap_tensorAdd F

theorem disjoint_splitLower_splitUpper (I : Box ι) (i : ι) (x : ℝ) :
    Disjoint (I.splitLower i x) (I.splitUpper i x) := by
  rw [← disjoint_withBotCoe, coe_splitLower, coe_splitUpper]
  refine (Disjoint.inf_left' _ ?_).inf_right' _
  rw [Set.disjoint_left]
  exact fun y (hle : y i ≤ x) hlt => not_lt_of_ge hle hlt

theorem splitLower_ne_splitUpper (I : Box ι) (i : ι) (x : ℝ) :
    I.splitLower i x ≠ I.splitUpper i x := by
  rcases le_or_gt x (I.lower i) with h | _
  · rw [splitUpper_eq_self.2 h, splitLower_eq_bot.2 h]
    exact WithBot.bot_ne_coe
  · refine (disjoint_splitLower_splitUpper I i x).ne ?_
    rwa [Ne, splitLower_eq_bot, not_le]

namespace Prepartition

variable {I J : Box ι} {i : ι} {x : ℝ}

open scoped Classical in
/-- The partition of `I : Box ι` into the boxes `I ∩ {y | y ≤ x i}` and `I ∩ {y | x i < y}`.
One of these boxes can be empty, then this partition is just the single-box partition `⊤`. -/
def split (I : Box ι) (i : ι) (x : ℝ) : Prepartition I :=
  ofWithBot {I.splitLower i x, I.splitUpper i x}
    (by
      simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton]
      rintro J (rfl | rfl)
      exacts [Box.splitLower_le, Box.splitUpper_le])
    (by
      simp only [Finset.coe_insert, Finset.coe_singleton, true_and, Set.mem_singleton_iff,
        pairwise_insert_of_symm, pairwise_singleton]
      rintro J rfl -
      exact I.disjoint_splitLower_splitUpper i x)

@[simp]
theorem mem_split_iff : J ∈ split I i x ↔ ↑J = I.splitLower i x ∨ ↑J = I.splitUpper i x := by
  simp [split]

theorem mem_split_iff' : J ∈ split I i x ↔
    (J : Set (ι → ℝ)) = ↑I ∩ { y | y i ≤ x } ∨ (J : Set (ι → ℝ)) = ↑I ∩ { y | x < y i } := by
  simp [mem_split_iff, ← Box.withBotCoe_inj]

@[simp]
theorem iUnion_split (I : Box ι) (i : ι) (x : ℝ) : (split I i x).iUnion = I := by
  simp [split, ← inter_union_distrib_left, ← setOf_or, le_or_gt]

theorem isPartitionSplit (I : Box ι) (i : ι) (x : ℝ) : IsPartition (split I i x) :=
  isPartition_iff_iUnion_eq.2 <| iUnion_split I i x

theorem sum_split_boxes {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (I : Box ι) (i : ι) (x : ℝ) (f : Box ι → M) :
    (∑ J ∈ (split I i x).boxes, f J) =
      (I.splitLower i x).elim' 0 f + (I.splitUpper i x).elim' 0 f := by
  classical
  rw [split, sum_ofWithBot, Finset.sum_pair (I.splitLower_ne_splitUpper i x)]

/-- If `x ∉ (I.lower i, I.upper i)`, then the hyperplane `{y | y i = x}` does not split `I`. -/
theorem split_of_notMem_Ioo (h : x ∉ Ioo (I.lower i) (I.upper i)) : split I i x = ⊤ := by
  refine ((isPartitionTop I).eq_of_boxes_subset fun J hJ => ?_).symm
  rcases mem_top.1 hJ with rfl; clear hJ
  rw [mem_boxes, mem_split_iff]
  rw [mem_Ioo, not_and_or, not_lt, not_lt] at h
  cases h <;> [right; left]
  · rwa [eq_comm, Box.splitUpper_eq_self]
  · rwa [eq_comm, Box.splitLower_eq_self]

theorem coe_eq_of_mem_split_of_mem_le {y : ι → ℝ} (h₁ : J ∈ split I i x) (h₂ : y ∈ J)
    (h₃ : y i ≤ x) : (J : Set (ι → ℝ)) = ↑I ∩ { y | y i ≤ x } := by
  refine (mem_split_iff'.1 h₁).resolve_right fun H => ?_
  rw [← Box.mem_coe, H] at h₂
  exact h₃.not_gt h₂.2

theorem coe_eq_of_mem_split_of_lt_mem {y : ι → ℝ} (h₁ : J ∈ split I i x) (h₂ : y ∈ J)
    (h₃ : x < y i) : (J : Set (ι → ℝ)) = ↑I ∩ { y | x < y i } := by
  refine (mem_split_iff'.1 h₁).resolve_left fun H => ?_
  rw [← Box.mem_coe, H] at h₂
  exact h₃.not_ge h₂.2

@[simp]
theorem restrict_split (h : I ≤ J) (i : ι) (x : ℝ) : (split J i x).restrict I = split I i x := by
  refine ((isPartitionSplit J i x).restrict h).eq_of_boxes_subset ?_
  simp only [Finset.subset_iff, mem_boxes, mem_restrict', mem_split_iff']
  have : ∀ s, (I ∩ s : Set (ι → ℝ)) ⊆ J := fun s => inter_subset_left.trans h
  rintro J₁ ⟨J₂, H₂ | H₂, H₁⟩ <;> [left; right] <;>
    simp [H₁, H₂, inter_left_comm (I : Set (ι → ℝ)), this]

theorem inf_split (π : Prepartition I) (i : ι) (x : ℝ) :
    π ⊓ split I i x = π.biUnion fun J => split J i x :=
  biUnion_congr_of_le rfl fun _ hJ => restrict_split hJ i x

/-- Split a box along many hyperplanes `{y | y i = x}`; each hyperplane is given by the pair
`(i x)`. -/
def splitMany (I : Box ι) (s : Finset (ι × ℝ)) : Prepartition I :=
  s.inf fun p => split I p.1 p.2

@[simp]
theorem splitMany_empty (I : Box ι) : splitMany I ∅ = ⊤ :=
  rfl

open scoped Classical in
@[simp]
theorem splitMany_insert (I : Box ι) (s : Finset (ι × ℝ)) (p : ι × ℝ) :
    splitMany I (insert p s) = splitMany I s ⊓ split I p.1 p.2 := by
  rw [splitMany, Finset.inf_insert, inf_comm, splitMany]

theorem splitMany_le_split (I : Box ι) {s : Finset (ι × ℝ)} {p : ι × ℝ} (hp : p ∈ s) :
    splitMany I s ≤ split I p.1 p.2 :=
  Finset.inf_le hp

theorem isPartition_splitMany (I : Box ι) (s : Finset (ι × ℝ)) : IsPartition (splitMany I s) := by
  classical
  exact Finset.induction_on s (by simp only [splitMany_empty, isPartitionTop]) fun a s _ hs => by

# Complete asymptotic invisibility via flat HT perturbations

- **ID:** asymptotic-flat-ht-invisibility
- **Stage:** 3-formalized/not_new_scientific_knowledge (third audit 2026-07-12)
- **Type:** CANDIDATE THEOREM
- **Source:** `ht-c09-asymptotic-scale-nontermination`; `finite-jet-nonidentifiability-ht`; Hölder; Stirling
- **Statement:** Arbitrary finite jets and any DA inverse-power Poincare asymptotic profile can be realized
  simultaneously by both a DA function and an HT function.

## Goal

Strengthen C09 from "no finite asymptotic prefix certifies HT" to a sharper obstruction:

> Even a complete classical asymptotic expansion, combined with arbitrary finite jet observations, does not
> distinguish DA from HT.

This is an anti-theatre theorem. Computations that fit many asymptotic terms, residual ranks, or local jets
cannot count as HT evidence unless they use a structural theorem outside the finite/asymptotic observation
functor.

## Multiplier lemma

Let `B` be a nonzero meromorphic function differentially algebraic over `C(z)`. Then

`B/Gamma`

is hypertranscendental over `C(z)`.

Indeed, if `B/Gamma` were DA, then `Gamma=B/(B/Gamma)` would be DA by field closure, contradicting Hölder.

Thus any nonzero DA multiplier `B` can transfer its ordinary analytic invisibility properties to an HT
perturbation. If `B` vanishes to prescribed finite orders, `B/Gamma` is invisible to those jets. If `B/Gamma`
is flat in an asymptotic scale, it is invisible to that scale. The theorem below chooses

`B(z)=lambda A(z)`

for finite jets and uses Stirling to get inverse-power flatness along `+infinity`; the DA correction
`e^(-z)Q` realizes arbitrary finite jet targets without changing the same asymptotic profile.

## Theorem `[PROVED HERE]`

Let `G` be a meromorphic function differentially algebraic over `C(z)`. Assume:

1. `G` is holomorphic at distinct points `a_1,...,a_N`;
2. `G` is holomorphic on the positive real ray for all sufficiently large `x`;
3. along `x -> +infinity`, `G(x)` admits a Poincare asymptotic expansion in inverse powers,

   `G(x) ~ sum_{n>=0} b_n x^{-n}`,

   meaning that for every `M`,

   `G(x)-sum_{n<M} b_n x^{-n} = o(x^{-M})`.

Fix arbitrary target jet values `c_{i,j}` for `1 <= i <= N`, `0 <= j <= m_i`.

Then there exist:

1. a meromorphic function `D` differentially algebraic over `C(z)`;
2. a punctured affine line of meromorphic functions `F_lambda`, `lambda in C^*`;

such that:

1. `D^(j)(a_i)=F_lambda^(j)(a_i)=c_{i,j}` for every `i,j`;
2. every `F_lambda` is hypertranscendental over `C(z)`;
3. `D` and every `F_lambda` have the same complete inverse-power Poincare asymptotic expansion as `G` along
   `+infinity`:

   `D(x) ~ F_lambda(x) ~ sum_{n>=0} b_n x^{-n}`.

The special case `G=0` says: every finite holomorphic jet table is realized by both a DA entire function and
an HT entire function whose complete inverse-power asymptotic expansion along `+infinity` is identically
zero.

## Construction

Choose a polynomial `Q` so that `E(z)=e^(-z)Q(z)` has the finite jets

`E^(j)(a_i)=c_{i,j}-G^(j)(a_i)`.

This is possible because multiplication by `e^(-z)` is an invertible linear map on each finite jet space, and
Hermite interpolation realizes the corresponding finite jets of `Q`.

Put

`A(z)=prod_i (z-a_i)^(m_i+1)`.

For every `lambda in C^*`, define

`D(z)=G(z)+E(z)`,

`F_lambda(z)=D(z)+lambda A(z)/Gamma(z)`.

## Proof

The jet agreement for `D` follows by construction of `Q`. The additional term `A/Gamma` has zeros of order
at least `m_i+1` at each `a_i`, so `F_lambda` has the same prescribed finite jets.

The function `E=e^(-z)Q` is D-finite, hence DA, and `D=G+E` is DA by closure of DA elements under field
operations.

For hypertranscendence, suppose `F_lambda` were differentially algebraic over `C(z)`. Since `D` is
differentially algebraic and DA elements form a field, the difference

`F_lambda-D=lambda A/Gamma`

would be differentially algebraic. Because `lambda A in C(z)^*`, this would make `1/Gamma` differentially
algebraic over `C(z)`, and hence `Gamma` differentially algebraic over `C(z)`, contradicting Hölder's theorem.
Thus `F_lambda` is HT.

It remains to check flatness. Since `Q` is a polynomial, `e^(-x)Q(x)=o(x^-M)` for every `M`. Stirling's formula
on the positive real axis gives

`Gamma(x) ~ sqrt(2*pi) x^(x-1/2) e^(-x)`.

For every fixed `M`, and for `d=deg A`,

`x^M A(x)/Gamma(x) -> 0`

because

`log |x^M A(x)/Gamma(x)| = (M+d) log x - (x-1/2) log x + x + O(1) -> -infinity`.

Therefore `A(x)/Gamma(x)=o(x^{-M})` for every `M`. Both added terms, `E` and `lambda A/Gamma`, are flat to all
orders in the inverse-power Poincare scale. Hence every truncation remainder for `G` remains a valid
truncation remainder for `D` and `F_lambda`. The complete asymptotic expansion is identical. ∎

# Asymptotic-type essential sewing law

Status: formalized.

## Statement

Let \(a\) be a nonvanishing asymptotic scale along an arbitrary filter.  Let \(f\) be
all-orders flat relative to \(a\), and let \(g\) have nonzero finite grade \(d\):
\[
 f=o(a^m)\quad(m\geq0),\qquad g=\Theta(a^d).
\]
Then the exact scalar sewing cost satisfies
\[
 a^{-K}=o(g/f)\qquad(K\geq0).
\]

More generally, for arbitrary real normed spaces \(E,F\), if \(f_x\in E\) is eventually
nonzero and all-orders flat, \(\|g_x\|=\Theta(a_x^d)\), and bounded linear maps
\(R_x:E\to F\) satisfy \(R_xf_x=g_x\), then
\[
 a_x^{-K}=o(\|R_x\|)\qquad(K\geq0).
\]

Thus an all-orders-flat germ and a nonzero finite-grade germ are different asymptotic species.
Exact sewing between them requires an essential scale singularity; finite dimension, infinite
rank, and matrix enlargement do not change the conclusion.

## Proof

At order \(K+d\), all-orders flatness gives
\[
 f=o(a^{K+d}).
\]
Inversion reverses the little-\(o\) relation, and multiplication by the finite-grade target gives
\[
 a^{-K}=o(g/f).
\]
For an exact bounded linear sewing,
\[
 \|g_x\|\leq\|R_x\|\,\|f_x\|,
\]
so the scalar norm ratio is \(O(\|R_x\|)\), proving the operator theorem.

## Public law

> **There is no single infinite future. Infinity is a geometric boundary,
> and different ways of waiting expose different dimensions of time.**

Shorter:

> **The infinite future has a shape.**

“Different ways of waiting” means different physically controlled joint
scalings of observation time, interaction strength, system size, resolution,
dissipation and other parameters. It does not mean that personal choice
changes an already fixed experiment.

## Frozen truth-hunch

For every physically admissible family of dynamical systems, its long-time
content is not correctly represented by one point called \(T=\infty\), nor by
any privileged order of limits. It has a canonical **asymptotic-time
boundary**
\[
  \partial_\infty\mathfrak T
\]
whose points or strata represent inequivalent scaling directions by which
physical observation approaches infinite time while other physical scales
degenerate, diverge or refine.

Every finite observation law extends to this boundary in a resolved form.
Different boundary strata may have different:

- observer-visible temporal dimension;
- recurrent phase group;
- persistent spectral mass;
- transient sector;
- return distribution;
- effective interaction connectivity;
- thermodynamic phase; and
- continuum completion.

The complete boundary, together with its incidence and transition laws, is
the invariant physical object. A sequential limit is only one boundary
chart.

This statement is frozen before selecting:

Standard asymptotic analysis asks which value a physical observable approaches

parameters. The conjecture reverses the role of the limit:

1. \(T=\infty\) is not a value but a boundary with internal geometry;
2. a long-time “phase” is a stratum of that boundary;
3. noncommuting limits are not pathologies to order away but evidence of
   distinct boundary directions;
4. crossover exponents are coordinates of the boundary;
5. temporal dimension is a local invariant of a boundary stratum;
6. a singular weak interaction may change the boundary topology while every
   bounded-time observable remains continuous;

Thus the infinite future is treated as physical asymptotic geometry, not as a
formal endpoint appended to finite time.

## Theorem-first derivation

Finite-divisor nonselection constructs an exact critical-line divisor prefix with a finite Euler
head and a fresh fixed orbit. Combined shadow blindness proves that multiplication by a free
reflection-orbit quartic preserves both finite Euler class and logarithmic-derivative tail. The
quartic is nonzero at every critical-line point, so the two interfaces compose without changing
any prescribed prefix multiplicity.

## Universal law

For every finite positive critical-line divisor with arbitrary multiplicities, every finite Euler
head, and every fresh fixed orbit, adjoining an arbitrary generic free off-line orbit preserves:

- the same finite Euler class;
- the exact full prescribed divisor prefix;
- the fresh fixed orbit with order one;
- eventual nonvanishing and the original asymptotic logarithmic-derivative tail.

The resulting carrier has order one and nontrivial level-one charge at the free off-line point.
Thus finite divisor data, finite exact Euler data, and the asymptotic tail are simultaneously blind
on one carrier.

## Paper proof

1. Use `finiteDivisorPrefix_orbitNonselection` for the fixed extension's finite Euler membership,
   prescribed multiplicities, and fresh order-one fixed orbit.
2. The fixed extension is eventually nonzero on a sufficiently far right half-plane: the Euler
   bundle is eventually nonzero and all critical-line factors are nonzero off `Re s = 1/2`.
3. Multiply it by `orbitQuartic ρ`. Apply `eventuallyNonvanishing_orbitQuartic_mul` and
   `dlogTail_orbitQuartic_mul`; absorb the quartic into the FE/Schwarz residual factor.
4. At old critical-line points and the fresh fixed point the quartic has order zero, so analytic
   order is unchanged.
5. At `ρ`, the fixed extension is nonzero and the quartic has simple order one, hence the new
   carrier has order one and level-one charge `-1`.

No numerical pre-certification applies: proof is exact divisor arithmetic and asymptotic-tail
invariance.

# Vanishing-mass finite-residue affine projective rigidity

- **ID:** `vanishing-mass-finite-residue-affine-projective-rigidity`
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** `THEOREM (Lean) / GENERAL HT SINGULARITY-CONSTRAINT LAW / NOVELTY UNVERIFIED`
- **Parent:** `../1-in-progress/vanishing-mass-finite-residue-projective-rigidity.md`
- **Lean:** `formal/GaloisForLFunctions/HTGeometry/VanishingMassResidueRigidity.lean`

## Theorem

Let `l` be a nontrivial asymptotic filter.  Let nonzero real masses `w_i` tend to zero, let
`epsilon_i,delta_i` be Boolean orientations, and suppose

```text
sign(delta_i) w_i = a sign(epsilon_i) w_i + q_i            (1)
```

eventually along `l`, where `a` is one real scalar and the correction sequence `q_i` has finite
range.  Then exactly one of the following holds:

```text
a = +1,  q_i = 0 eventually,  epsilon_i = delta_i eventually;
a = -1,  q_i = 0 eventually,  epsilon_i != delta_i eventually. (2)
```

More generally, if

```text
q_i = sum_j c_j n_j(i),
```

with finitely many coefficients `c_j` and each integer-valued order function `n_j` having finite
range, then `q` has finite range and the same conclusion follows.

## Mechanism

Rearranging `(1)` expresses `q_i` as a uniformly bounded signed coefficient times `w_i`, so
`q_i -> 0`.  A finite-range map into a `T1` space which converges to zero is eventually zero.
Cancelling the nonzero mass leaves an equality between two Boolean signs under the single scalar
`a`, forcing `a=+1` or `a=-1` globally and therefore the corresponding projective tail relation.

This is a positive maximal-class statement: every finite quantized residue correction is screened
by a vanishing mass palette, and the surviving asymptotic symmetry is exactly the global
projective sign.

## Universal prime-log specialization

The actual universal prime-log masses are positive and summable, hence tend to zero on the
cofinite prime filter.  The theorem therefore proves that any affine residue action with a finite
correction palette preserving those signed masses must relate the two prime orientations by
eventual equality or eventual opposition.  The conclusion is exactly
`PrimeOrientationTailPairDependent` through the existing projective-tail classification.

This does not yet prove that every differential-field re-expression induces a finite-range
correction.  That local-to-global differential-birational rigidity statement remains isolated in
the parent card.

## Physical lens

`[CONJECTURAL INTERPRETATION]` The masses behave as oscillator strengths tending to zero, while the
finite correction palette behaves as finitely many quantized winding charges from logarithmic
derivatives.  The theorem says that vanishing-strength channels asymptotically screen every fixed
finite charge palette; only a global `Z/2` superselection sector survives.  This interpretation is
a source of candidate laws, not part of the mathematical claim.

## RH route constraint

Any route that encodes prime data in this summable signed pole palette and changes carriers only by
one affine scalar plus finitely generated bounded logarithmic residue charges must preserve the
prime orientation tail up to global sign.  A route capable of independent asymptotic prime sign
surgery must therefore use an infinite correction palette, unbounded pole-order data, or a truly
non-affine singularity action.

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.QuantumRecurrenceCoronaLaw

/-!
# Finite-observation / asymptotic-completion separation

Every finite cylinder of complete histories projects onto the whole recurrence
corona.  Consequently, a reporter on asymptotic history classes that is
determined by any fixed finite observation horizon is constant.

This is an exact information boundary: no nonconstant complete-time spectral
invariant can be an exact finite-horizon observable.
-/

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

open GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- The recurrence-asymptotic relation ignores every finite modification of
a history. -/
theorem recurrenceAsymptoticSetoid_tailSaturated :
    TailSaturated recurrenceAsymptoticSetoid := by
  intro u v huv
  exact (recurrenceCoronaClass_eq_iff u v).mp
    (recurrenceCoronaClass_eq_of_eventuallyEq huv)

/-- A recurrence-corona reporter is determined by horizon `N` when histories
agreeing through `N` always receive the same reported value. -/
def RecurrenceCoronaReporterDeterminedBy
    {Y : Type*} (N : ℕ) (F : RecurrenceCorona → Y) : Prop :=
  ∀ u v : ℕ → ℂ,
    (∀ n ≤ N, u n = v n) →
      F (recurrenceCoronaClass u) = F (recurrenceCoronaClass v)

/-- **Finite-observation / asymptotic-completion separation law.** Every map
from the recurrence corona that is determined by one finite observation
horizon is constant. -/
theorem finiteHorizon_recurrenceCoronaReporter_constant
    {Y : Type*} (N : ℕ) (F : RecurrenceCorona → Y)
    (hF : RecurrenceCoronaReporterDeterminedBy N F) :
    ReporterConstant F := by
  intro q₁ q₂
  obtain ⟨u, rfl⟩ := Quotient.exists_rep q₁
  obtain ⟨w, hprefix, hw⟩ :=
    finiteCylinder_surjective_recurrenceCorona N u q₂
  rw [← hw]
  exact hF u w fun n hn => (hprefix n hn).symm

/-- Every nonconstant recurrence-corona reporter necessarily escapes every
fixed finite observation horizon. -/
theorem nonconstant_recurrenceCoronaReporter_not_determinedBy
    {Y : Type*} (F : RecurrenceCorona → Y)
    (hF : ¬ ReporterConstant F) (N : ℕ) :
    ¬ RecurrenceCoronaReporterDeterminedBy N F := by
  intro hfinite
  exact hF (finiteHorizon_recurrenceCoronaReporter_constant N F hfinite)

/-- No finite-horizon-determined reporter can injectively encode the
recurrence corona. -/
theorem finiteHorizon_recurrenceCoronaReporter_not_injective
    {Y : Type*} (N : ℕ) (F : RecurrenceCorona → Y)
    (hF : RecurrenceCoronaReporterDeterminedBy N F) :
    ¬ Function.Injective F := by
  intro hinjective
  have hconstant := finiteHorizon_recurrenceCoronaReporter_constant N F hF
  apply recurrenceCoronaClass_postHorizonPersistentHistory_ne_zero N
  apply hinjective
  exact hconstant _ _

end

end RHTower

# Combined germ-blindness: exact finite Euler data and the asymptotic tail, on one witness

Two independent blindness mechanisms are united here on a *single* carrier.  The finite-Euler head
`feBundle P` is divisor-inert on the strip (`FiniteEulerInert`): decorating a member by it changes no
strip vanishing order, so exact finite local Euler data carries no divisor constraint.  The
logarithmic-derivative tail is quartic-blind (`TailBlindness`): multiplying by the `V₄`-orbit quartic
of an off-line point leaves the asymptotic tail `deriv f / f` unchanged toward `re → ∞`, so an
asymptotic tiling condition sees no off-line surgery.

The doubly-decorated class `ShadowClass P F` collects the carriers that simultaneously carry the exact
`P`-Euler head (`FiniteEulerClass P`), stay eventually nonvanishing, and match a fixed tail reference
`F` (`DlogTail F`).  Its softness combines the two mechanisms on one witness: from any member `f₀`
that is nonvanishing at an off-line point `ρ`, one orbit-quartic multiplication `g = orbitQuartic ρ · f₀`
lands back in the *same* class — same finite exact Euler head, same asymptotic tail — yet raises the
order at `ρ` to `1`, so `g` carries off-line deck charge `−1` (`shadowClass_charged_witness`).  Taking
the finite Euler bundle itself as the base member (`ShadowClass P (feBundle P) (feBundle P)`, with
eventual nonvanishing on the right half-plane and the trivial self-tail) yields the capstone
`not_forcesRHParity_shadowClass`: the class matching exactly `feBundle P` in both its finite Euler data
and its logarithmic-derivative tail carries off-line charge, hence cannot force RH-grade parity.

No criterion that reads finite exact local Euler data joined with asymptotic tail data can force
RH-grade parity: both faces are simultaneously blind on a single object.  Any parity-forcing content of
the Euler germ is consumed only at the whole-object, non-asymptotic level — not in any finite truncation
and not in the asymptotic tail.
-/

namespace RHTower

/-! ### §1 The doubly-decorated class -/

finite `P`-Euler head, are eventually nonvanishing, and match the fixed logarithmic-derivative tail
reference `F`.  A member holds exact finite local Euler data *and* a prescribed asymptotic tail. -/
def ShadowClass (P : Finset ℕ) (F : ℂ → ℂ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) : Prop :=
  FiniteEulerClass P f ∧ EventuallyNonvanishing f ∧ DlogTail F f

/-! ### §2 The finite Euler bundle is a member of its own shadow class -/

/-- **The inverse Euler factor is zero-free on the left half-plane.**  For `Re w < 0` and `p > 1` one
has `‖exp(−w·log p)‖ = exp(−Re w·log p) > 1`, so `exp(−w·log p) ≠ 1` and `1 − exp(−w·log p) ≠ 0`.

theorem eulerInvFactor_ne_zero_of_re_neg (p : ℕ) (hp : 1 < p) {w : ℂ} (hw : w.re < 0) :
    eulerInvFactor p w ≠ 0 := by
  intro h

  have hE : Complex.exp (-(w * (Real.log p : ℂ))) = 1 := (sub_eq_zero.mp h).symm
  have hnorm : ‖Complex.exp (-(w * (Real.log p : ℂ)))‖ = 1 := by rw [hE, norm_one]
  rw [Complex.norm_exp] at hnorm
  have hre : (-(w * (Real.log p : ℂ))).re = -(w.re * Real.log p) := by
    rw [Complex.neg_re, Complex.mul_re, Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.ofReal_im, mul_zero, sub_zero]
  rw [hre] at hnorm

  refine eulerInvFactor_ne_zero_of_re_neg p (hP p hp) ?_

/-- Every function matches its own logarithmic-derivative tail: the difference `deriv f / f − deriv F / F`
is identically `0` when `F = f`, so `DlogTail f f` holds vacuously. -/
theorem dlogTail_self (F : ℂ → ℂ) : DlogTail F F := by
  intro ε hε
  refine ⟨0, fun s _ => ?_⟩
  rw [sub_self, norm_zero]; exact hε

  exists_cutoff_not_memSchattenClass T prime
    (fun N hN => memWeakSchattenClass_of_tendsto_mul_succ (hasymp N hN))
    (fun N hN => hasSchattenLogResidue_of_tendsto_mul_succ (hasymp N hN)) q hq

/-- The finite-prime aperture census law, with its two endpoint certificates replaced by the

theorem finitePrimeAperture_cuspDivisorSchattenRankUniversality_of_asymptotic
    (N : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ Nat.primeCounting N)
    (prime : Fin (Nat.primeCounting N) → Nat.Primes)
    (T : H →L[ℂ] H)
    (hasymp : Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ =>
        approxNumber T n ^ ((gaussPairedCriticalDepth N : ℕ) : ℝ) * ((n : ℝ) + 1))
      atTop (nhds (gaussPairedChannelResidue (Nat.primeCounting N) prime)))

    (kappa : ℕ) (V D : Submodule ℚ E)
    (hV : Module.finrank ℚ ↥V = Nat.primeCounting N)
    (hstate : Module.finrank ℚ (↥V ⧸ Submodule.comap V.subtype D) ≤ 2 * kappa) :

/-!
# The boundary at infinity of the observer-metric space

A traceless Hermitian direction generates the ray `t ↦ exp (t T)` of observer metrics.  Two rays
are asymptotic when their distance stays bounded, and the asymptote class of a ray, based at the
reference metric, is exactly its degeneration flag:

```text
Asymptotic (ray T) (ray S)  ↔  ∀ c, eigenSum T c = eigenSum S c.
```

The forward direction is the exponential metric increasing property — distinct directions diverge
linearly, so a bounded distance forces equality — and the backward direction is that a Hermitian
direction is determined by its flag.  Since the flags are the simplices of the horizon building,
this is the card's metric-degeneration dictionary as an equivalence: the boundary point of a ray
carries exactly the information of a flag, no more and no less.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open Module

variable {E : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℂ E] [FiniteDimensional ℂ E]

/-! ## Rays and the asymptote relation -/

/-- The ray of observer metrics generated by a Hermitian direction. -/
noncomputable def observerRay {T : E →ₗ[ℂ] E} (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (t : ℝ) : ObserverMetric E where
  form := (metricRay T t : E →ₗ[ℂ] E)
  isSymm := isSymmetric_metricRay hT rfl t
  isPos := fun _ hv => inner_metricRay_pos hT rfl hv t

/-- Two rays are asymptotic when the distance between them stays bounded. -/
def Asymptotic (γ δ : ℝ → ObserverMetric E) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → dist (γ t) (δ t) ≤ C

theorem asymptotic_refl (γ : ℝ → ObserverMetric E) : Asymptotic γ γ :=
  ⟨0, fun t _ => le_of_eq (dist_self (γ t))⟩

theorem Asymptotic.symm {γ δ : ℝ → ObserverMetric E} (h : Asymptotic γ δ) : Asymptotic δ γ := by
  obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := h
  exact ⟨C, fun t ht => by rw [dist_comm]; exact hC t ht⟩

theorem Asymptotic.trans {γ δ ε : ℝ → ObserverMetric E} (h₁ : Asymptotic γ δ)
    (h₂ : Asymptotic δ ε) : Asymptotic γ ε := by
  obtain ⟨C₁, hC₁⟩ := h₁
  obtain ⟨C₂, hC₂⟩ := h₂
  exact ⟨C₁ + C₂, fun t ht =>
    le_trans (dist_triangle (γ t) (δ t) (ε t)) (add_le_add (hC₁ t ht) (hC₂ t ht))⟩

theorem dist_observerRay {T S : E →ₗ[ℂ] E} (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hS : S.IsSymmetric) (t : ℝ) :
    dist (observerRay hT t) (observerRay hS t)
      = observerDist (isSymmetric_metricRay hT rfl t) rfl (isSymmetric_metricRay hS rfl t) :=
  rfl

/-! ## Distinct traceless directions are not asymptotic -/

/-- **Rays with distinct traceless directions are not asymptotic.**  Their distance grows at least
linearly, by the exponential metric increasing property. -/
theorem not_asymptotic_observerRay {T S : E →ₗ[ℂ] E} (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hS : S.IsSymmetric)
    (htr : LinearMap.trace ℂ E (S - T) = 0) (hne : S ≠ T) :
    ¬ Asymptotic (observerRay hT) (observerRay hS) := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc, hbound⟩ := exists_pos_le_observerDist_metricRay hT hS rfl htr hne
  rintro ⟨C, hC⟩
  have ht : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (|C| + 1) / c := by positivity
  have h1 := hbound ((|C| + 1) / c) ht
  have h2 := hC ((|C| + 1) / c) ht
  rw [dist_observerRay] at h2
  have hcc : c * ((|C| + 1) / c) = |C| + 1 := by field_simp
  rw [hcc] at h1
  have : |C| + 1 ≤ C := le_trans h1 h2
  linarith [le_abs_self C]

/-! ## The asymptote class is the degeneration flag -/

/-- **The asymptote class of a ray is its degeneration flag.**  Two rays of traceless directions
are asymptotic exactly when their flags agree at every threshold.  Since the flags are the
simplices of the horizon building, the boundary point of a ray carries exactly the data of a flag.
-/
theorem asymptotic_iff_eigenSum_eq {T S : E →ₗ[ℂ] E} (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hS : S.IsSymmetric)
    (htr : LinearMap.trace ℂ E (S - T) = 0) :
    Asymptotic (observerRay hT) (observerRay hS) ↔ ∀ c : ℝ, eigenSum T c = eigenSum S c := by
  constructor
  · intro h c
    by_cases hne : S = T
    · rw [hne]
    · exact absurd h (not_asymptotic_observerRay hT hS htr hne)
  · intro h
    have hST : S = T := eq_of_eigenSum_eq hS hT rfl fun c => (h c).symm
    subst hST
    exact asymptotic_refl _

/-- **The boundary at infinity, based at the reference metric, is faithfully labelled by
directions.**  Distinct traceless directions give distinct asymptote classes. -/
theorem eq_of_asymptotic {T S : E →ₗ[ℂ] E} (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hS : S.IsSymmetric)
    (htr : LinearMap.trace ℂ E (S - T) = 0)
    (h : Asymptotic (observerRay hT) (observerRay hS)) : S = T := by
  by_contra hne
  exact not_asymptotic_observerRay hT hS htr hne h
